hold_text: Tier-2 SIGNAL PATH: src/runtime/pipeline.py and src/runtime/intent_multiplexer.py are src/** runtime, so this cannot self-land whatever its approval state. THE CHANGE ITSELF IS ALREADY APPROVED and must NOT be re-asked: the operator was put the question on 2026-09-09 (DEC-20260909-ROLLBACK-BUILDER-REGISTRY on WO-20260909-DECISION-THE-ROLLBACK-REGISTRY-IS-AN-OUTAGE) and chose `collapse_to_one_registry` over the three alternatives, one of which was the parity test alone. What is owed is the merge click, and one human read of the safety argument, which is a single claim and is measured rather than argued: the deleted registry was a STRICT SUBSET of the surviving roster and all 16 of its names mapped to the IDENTICAL builder object, compared by `is` and not by name, so for the legs that worked under the rollback the callable is byte-identical and for the 35 that did not it goes from skipped to built. The reviewer's check is that identity claim, not the diff's size. TWO THINGS THIS DOES NOT DO, deliberately. (1) It does not flip MULTI_STRATEGY_INTENT_LAYER on any VM, and must not be read as a request to: the flag is default-on, the live path is unchanged by this diff, and the rollback path this repairs is not currently selected on the fleet. (2) It does not touch the intent layer's aggregation, priorities, gating or order path -- only WHICH roster the rollback entry point resolves against. ⚠️ ONE REAL CONSEQUENCE TO WEIGH, stated rather than buried: if the rollback IS exercised in future it now evaluates 55 builders per tick where it used to evaluate 16, so a tick under the rollback becomes more expensive. That is the point (the 39 were live legs going unbuilt) and it is bounded by the fact that the default path already evaluates all 55 today, but it is a real change to what the rollback costs and a reviewer should see it said out loud.
why: Audit F-28, built as MI-229 under WO-20260909-DECISION-THE-ROLLBACK-REGISTRY-IS-AN-OUTAGE. Deletes pipeline._STRATEGY_BUILDERS, the SECOND strategy->builder registry, and routes multiplexed_signal_builder + monitor_unit_for through intent_multiplexer._resolve_builders(). MEASURED HERE BEFORE THE CHANGE rather than transcribed, and the audit's figures reproduced exactly (population: all 55 strategies declared in config/strategies.yaml, of which 45 are execution:live) -- 55 names in the intent roster, 16 in pipeline's, 39 missing, 35 of them live, i.e. 78%. Because MULTI_STRATEGY_INTENT_LAYER=false is documented in run_pipeline as the no-redeploy rollback and routed to the 16, the sanctioned rollback was a 78% capability outage presenting as one logger.warning per leg per tick. After the collapse the rollback path builds 45 of 45 live legs, up from 10 of 45. ALSO SHIPS THE RECURRENCE DETECTOR the operator's answer asks for (tests/test_strategy_builder_registry_single_home.py, 7 tests): an AST scan for a `name -> *_signal_builder` dict literal anywhere under src/, carrying its OWN POSITIVE CONTROL so a scan that has silently stopped matching cannot pass as a clean result; a behavioural test that swaps the single home's roster and requires the ROLLBACK path to be observed firing the swapped builder; and the F-28 measurement re-run as an assertion. PLANTED-CONTROL EVIDENCE, three plants, each reverted: a 3-entry dict re-added to pipeline fails 2 of 7; a module-local dict inside multiplexed_signal_builder fails the behavioural test; a local dict in monitor_unit_for (the pre-2026-06 BL-20260615-MGCNAKED shape) fails 2 of 7. ⚠️ ONE OF MY OWN TESTS WAS WRONG AND WAS FIXED, not worked around: the first behavioural test asserted side=='none' against a roster with no real names, and PASSED under plant A -- the real turtle_soup builder also returns none on a bare settings dict, so it was green for the wrong reason. Rewritten to register the sentinel under a REAL strategy name and require it to be OBSERVED FIRING. Also updates the seven tests that named the deleted symbol -- onto a new per-call `builders=` kwarg mirroring multiplexed_intent_signal_builder's, or onto intent_multiplexer._REGISTERED_BUILDERS, the sanctioned extension point -- and the three docs that INSTRUCTED authors to register in the deleted dict (.claude/skills/new-strategy/SKILL.md step 3, docs/strategies/supported_strategies.md step 2, docs/strategies/ict_scalp_5m.md). That instruction is the drift mechanism, not a cosmetic reference: it was skippable with no observable consequence on the live path, which is exactly why 39 authors skipped it. Deliberately NOT touched: src/units/accounts/execute.py and scripts/ops/system_invariants.py (MI-227 live in both). No order placed, modified or cancelled; no env var changed on any VM.
